title: Directed Cellular Self-Assembly to Fabricate Cell-Derived Tissue Rings for Biomechanical Analysis and Tissue Engineering
protocol: Mill a 1/2" thick piece of polycarbonate to create round-bottomed annular wells with center post diameter of 2 mm, channels 6 mm deep and 3.75 mm wide.
Clean and dry the polycarbonate mold.
Mix polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) at a 10:1 ratio (w/w) of base to curing agent.
Degas the PDMS mixture to remove air bubbles.
Pour the degassed PDMS onto the polycarbonate mold.
Degas again to remove any remaining bubbles.
Cure the PDMS in the oven at 60°C for 4 hours.
Peel the cured PDMS template away from the polycarbonate carefully.
Wash the PDMS template with soap and water.
Autoclave the PDMS template.
Prepare a solution of two percent agarose (w/v) dissolved in Dulbecco's modified Eagle medium (DMEM).
Autoclave the agarose-DMEM solution.
Place the PDMS template on a level surface.
Fill each center post mold and surrounding space with molten agarose using pipettes.
Allow the agarose to solidify for approximately 15 minutes.
Invert the mold to release the agarose from the PDMS.
Cut excess agarose around each of the wells.
Place the agarose wells into 12-well plates.
Add cell culture media (DMEM with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin) around the outside of the agarose mold without covering the top of the molds.
Allow the plates to equilibrate in the incubator for approximately 15 minutes while preparing the cells.
Trypsinize rat aortic smooth muscle cells (rSMCs) when they reach 90% confluence.
Resuspend trypsinized rSMCs at a concentration of 5x10^6 cells/ml.
Pipette 100 μL of cell suspension into each annular agarose well using a circular motion.
Place the plates in the incubator and allow them to sit undisturbed for 24 hours.
Exchange medium every two days by aspirating media from around the wells and refilling with fresh medium until the agarose well is completely submerged.
Remove the ring from the agarose mold by sliding it over the center post at the conclusion of culture.
Place the ring in a small Petri dish with phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Acquire an image using a digital imaging system for edge detection.
Measure thickness at 4 positions around the circumference of the ring.
Calculate mean thickness value (t) and cross-sectional area (2π(t/2)^2) for each individual ring.
Set up the tensile testing machine in horizontal position.
Attach a 1N ±1mN load cell to the tensile testing machine.
Use custom thin wire grips created by bending stainless steel wire.
Mount the ring sample on two thin wire grips.
Extend the grips until a 5 mN tare load is applied to the sample.
Enter the cross-sectional area into the system and record the gauge length.
Pre-cycle the rings 8 times between the tare load and 50 kPa stress at a rate of 10 mm/min.
Pull to failure at 10 mm/min after the eighth pre-cycle.
Note failure as a decrease in force by 40% from one measurement to the next.
Measure the ultimate tensile stress (UTS) and failure strain for each ring sample.
Calculate the maximum tangent modulus (MTM) from the acquired data.
Fabricate custom tube holders from round polycarbonate disks with rectangular cutouts.
Drill threaded holes through the disks to allow two holders to be screwed together.
Autoclave the custom tube holders.
Place autoclaved custom tube holders in an empty Petri dish in a biosafety cabinet.
Cut ends of 1.9 mm diameter silicone tubes at an angle to create beveled edges.
Autoclave the beveled-edge silicone tubes.
Fill a Petri dish with media while the tubes are being autoclaved.
Remove rings from agarose wells and place them in the Petri dish with media.
Place autoclaved silicone tubes in the same Petri dish to wet them before use.
Use forceps to place a beveled end of a silicone tube into the center of a ring.
Gently slide the ring onto the silicone tubing.
Repeat placing and sliding rings as desired.
Slide the rings into contact with one another by gently pushing them successively in both directions along the tube.
Align silicone tubes within the polycarbonate holders.
Screw the two parts of the holder together.
Place the holder in a 100 mm Petri dish.
Add 55 ml media to the dish.
Exchange media every 3 days for the duration of culture.
Release the silicone tubes from the polycarbonate holder.
Use forceps to slide the tissue tubes off the silicone tube and into a Petri dish filled with PBS.
